plan.title: Colon RSEM bulk RNA-seq: 6 treated vs 6 control DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The counts matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples plus 1 gene-symbol column) holds RSEM gene-level expected counts — non-integer values — for 6 treated vs 6 control colon samples, unpaired, single batch. The delivered matrix lacks the per-sample effective-length information that a proper tximport-rsem import would use as a length offset, so the standard tximport(type='rsem') path (rule R-0065) cannot be executed as specified; the plan uses DESeq2's documented fallback of rounding the expected counts to the nearest integer and states this substitution explicitly as a caveat rather than silently applying the ideal method. sample_01's library size (~4x below median) is kept through QC, inspected on PCA/sample-distance/library-size plots, and removed only if the QC step gives a concrete, stated reason (e.g., extreme outlier or failed clustering) — not by default. The core comparison is fit with DESeq2 (Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, BH-adjusted independent filtering, alpha=0.05), cross-checked with edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as a second method, reporting the intersection as the high-confidence gene set per knowledge-service guidance for this replicate range (n=6/6). Enrichment runs fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against the locally staged MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets, followed by Reactome and WikiPathways human pathway sets as second-pass collections, all confirmed present in the reference store. A final report step consolidates fit diagnostics, gene tables (raw + shrunken LFC), the DE-method overlap, enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions, seeds).
